options.title: Titan Submersible: Its Last Text Came From 3,363 m Down
options.first_line: The Titan submersible sent its last text from three thousand three hundred and sixty-three metres down.
options.first_frame: Titan in 3D sinking through black water with its lamps on, the support ship's depth readout beside it ticking past 3,300 m, a date caption and the reconstruction tag

options.title: What Happened to the Titan Sub After Its Last Message?
options.first_line: June 2023: the Titan submersible sends one last message to its ship. What happens next?
options.first_frame: the support ship's control screen with a chat window, Titan's last message landing in it, and Titan in 3D sinking in the dark behind the glass

options.title: Titan's Last Message Was Routine. Then the Sub Went Silent.
options.first_line: Titan's last message was routine: it had dropped two weights. Then the sub went silent.
options.first_frame: Titan in 3D close up in the dark, two steel weights falling away from its frame, a text bubble DROPPED TWO WTS over it, the reconstruction tag

why: A famous sub whose last message was ordinary and then went silent raises a real how-is-that-possible question the title doesn't answer, where A's depth figure only states a big number and B leans on a 'what happens next?' tease, and C's first frame (weights dropping, DROPPED TWO WTS) reads clearly with the sound off.
